slides.heading: Health Care Delivery System
slides.subtitle: The totality of societal services designed to protect or restore health — plus newborn screening.

slides.heading: Newborn Screening (RA 9288)
bullets: Done after 24 hours of life via heel prick (lateral).
Detects genetic disorders to prevent complications and premature death.

terms.definition: Defect in branched-chain amino acid metabolism.

slides.heading: Expanded NBS
bullets: Includes cystic fibrosis, organic acid disorders, amino acid disorders, fatty acid disorders.

slides.heading: Two Sectors of the System
bullets: Public sector — tax-financed (national & local); care generally free at point of service.
Private sector — market-oriented; care paid through user fees at point of service.
Devolution under the Local Government Code (1991) reorganized the national health system.

slides.heading: Levels of Health Care
rows: First contact; basic services & traditional healers.
Complicated cases & intensive care by specialists.

terms.definition: Satellite/extension station; manned by Public Health Midwife (PHM) and BHWs.
Main/intermediate center with the complete health care team.
Frontline = PHM; supervisor = PHN; manager = RHP; plus sanitary inspector, medtech, dentist.

slides.heading: Primary Health Care Workers
bullets: Village/BHWs — trained community health workers, health auxiliary volunteers, or traditional birth attendants/healers.
Intermediate-level workers — general medical practitioners/assistants, PHNs, rural sanitary inspectors, midwives.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Newborn screening: RA 9288, heel prick after 24 h; basic = 6, expanded = 28 disorders.
System has a public (tax-funded, free) and private (user-fee) sector.
Three care levels: primary (BHS/RHU) → secondary → tertiary.
PHN ratio 1:10,000; care devolved under the LGU Code (1991).
